# Overview {visibility="hidden"}

# Two-species models



# Community occupancy models

## Community occupancy model

Species may go undetected for a couple reason:

::: {.incremental}
1. They are rare and are not present in our sample
2. They are present in our sample but are cryptic
:::

<br>

::: {.fragment}
Older methods like rarefaction attempt to address the first issue but not the second. 
:::

::: {.fragment}
We have to address both issues to obtain unbiased estimates of community parameters like species richness. 
:::



## Community occupancy model

::: {style='font-size: 75%;'}
Occupancy of species $i$ present at site $j$?

$$
  z_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_i)
$$

::: {.fragment}
Detection data for species $i$ at site $j$ on occasion $k$?

$$
  y_{ijk} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_{ij} \times p_i)
$$
:::

<br>

::: {.fragment}
Species-specific effects can be modeled as functions of covariates and/or regarded as random. Here's an example without covariates:

$$
  \mathrm{logit}(\psi_j) \sim \mathrm{Norm}(\mu_{\psi}, \sigma^2_{\psi})
$$

$$
  \mathrm{logit}(p_j) \sim \mathrm{Norm}(\mu_{p}, \sigma^2_{p})
$$

:::
:::



## Species richness

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
What do we do if we don't know how many species are in the community?

::: {.fragment}
Two options:
:::

::: {.fragment}
1. Model only the species that were in the sample.
    * This won't let you estimate actual richness, but it will let you account for species (in the sample) that were present but not detected at some sites.
:::

::: {.fragment}
2. Estimate the number of species that were *not* detected in the sample.
    * This can be accomplished using data augmentation.
    * Ideally, we would use some sort of "species checklist" to focus on species that *could have been present*. 
:::

:::



## Simulation without covariates

::: {style='font-size: 80%;'}
```{r}
#| label: sim-mso-nocov
#| code-line-numbers: "1-3|5-9|11-14|16-24"

N <- 50    # n_species
J <- 40    # n_sites
K <- 3     # n_visits

## Occupancy as logit-normal random effects 
set.seed(34020)
mu_logit_psi <- -2
sd_logit_psi <- 1
psi <- plogis(rnorm(n=N, mean=mu_logit_psi, sd=sd_logit_psi))

## Detection prob as logit-normal random effects
mu_logit_p <- -1
sd_logit_p <- 0.5
p <- plogis(rnorm(n=N, mean=mu_logit_p, sd=sd_logit_p))

## Occupancy and data
z <- matrix(NA, nrow=N, ncol=J) # latent occupancy state for species i at site j
yall <- array(NA, dim=c(N,J,K)) # Data (except we don't know spp that weren't detected)
for(i in 1:N) {
  z[i,] <- rbinom(n=J, size=1, prob=psi[i])
  for(j in 1:J) {
    yall[i,j,] <- rbinom(n=K, size=1, prob=z[i,j]*p[i])
  }
}
```
:::



## Simulation without covariates


::: {style='font-size: 70%;'}
```{r}
#| label: psi-re
#| output-location: column
hist(psi, xlab="Species-level occupancy",
     cex.lab=1.5)
```


```{r}
#| label: p-re
#| output-location: column
hist(p, xlab="Species-level detection probability",
     cex.lab=1.5)
```
:::



## Simulation without covariates


Notice that some species were not detected, and thus can't be part of the dataset. 

```{r}
#| label: missed-spp

detected <- rowSums(yall)>0
table(detected)

y <- yall[detected,,] # Discard species that weren't detected




```



## JAGS model pretending we know all the species


```{r}
#| label: comm-occ-knownN
#| echo: false
writeLines(readLines("comm-occ-knownN.jag"))
```


## JAGS model pretending we know all the species


```{r}
#| label: jags-fit-knownN
#| output-location: slide
#| results: hide
library(jagsUI)
jd_fixedN <- list(y=y, n_species=nrow(y), n_sites=ncol(y), n_occasions=dim(y)[3])
jp_fixedN <- c("mu_logit_psi", "sd_logit_psi", "mu_logit_p", "sd_logit_p")
ji_fixedN <- function() list(mu_logit_psi=rnorm(1), sd_logit_psi=rexp(1),
                             mu_logit_p=rnorm(1), sd_logit_p=rexp(1),
                             z=matrix(1, nrow=nrow(y), ncol=ncol(y)))

post_fixedN <- jags.basic(data=jd_fixedN, inits=ji_fixedN, parameters.to.save=jp_fixedN,
                          model.file="comm-occ-knownN.jag", n.chains=1, n.iter=2000)

plot(post_fixedN)
```




## JAGS model estimating richness


```{r}
#| label: comm-occ-unknownN
#| echo: false
writeLines(readLines("comm-occ-unknownN.jag"))
```



## JAGS model estimating richness


```{r}
#| label: jags-fit-unknownN
#| output-location: slide
#| results: hide
M <- 100
y_aug <- array(0, c(M,J,K))
y_aug[1:nrow(y),,] <- y

jd_unknownN <- list(y=y_aug, M=M, n_sites=ncol(y), n_occasions=dim(y)[3])
jp_unknownN <- c("mu_logit_psi", "sd_logit_psi", "mu_logit_p", "sd_logit_p", "N")
ji_unknownN <- function() list(mu_logit_psi=rnorm(1), sd_logit_psi=0.1,
                               mu_logit_p=rnorm(1), sd_logit_p=0.1,
                               w=rep(1, M), z=matrix(1, nrow=M, ncol=ncol(y)))

post_unknownN <- jags.basic(data=jd_unknownN, inits=ji_unknownN,
                            parameters.to.save=jp_unknownN,
                            model.file="comm-occ-unknownN.jag", n.chains=1, n.iter=5000)

plot(post_unknownN)
```
